caption: The drawing depicts a single handheld bell with a brown wooden handle and a brass-colored metallic body. The handle is smooth, elongated, and tapers slightly towards the top, where the number "12" is engraved or marked near the top surface. The body of the bell is wide at the base and narrows towards the neck where it connects to the handle; the base is wider and has a rounded, slightly chamfered edge. The metallic surface of the bell shows a bronze or brass coloring with some areas of shading to give the appearance of dimensionality and metallic reflection. There is an inscription in capital letters visible on the body of the bell, though not all of the text is clearly legible. The bell is the sole object on an off-white or light beige background, and the artist's signature “Edith Turner” is located in the bottom right corner of the image.
title: Town Crier's Bell
